# Contracts (MVP)

The interfaces between the three [work packages](work-packages.md). If something here doesn't fit, raise it with the team before coding around it.

## Stack

| Part | Choice |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend (iPhone) | SwiftUI, iOS 17+, `URLSessionWebSocketTask`, `AVAudioEngine`, [a2ui-swift](https://github.com/BBC6BAE9/a2ui-swift) `from: "0.3.0"` (product `A2UISwiftUI`) |
| Backend | Python 3.11, uv, FastAPI and uvicorn, httpx, `google-genai`, `gradium`, python-dotenv, pytest |
| Hosting | Server on a dev Mac; a Cloudflare quick tunnel gives the HTTPS and WSS URL that the app and the Shortcut use. Start it once and leave it running: the URL changes on every restart |
| Time zone | `Europe/Zurich` everywhere; times on the wire are ISO 8601 with offset |

```text
frontend/               # WP1: Xcode project, SwiftUI
backend/                # run from here: uv run uvicorn app:app --reload --port 8000
  pyproject.toml        # WP2 owns it; lists every package's deps
  .env.example
  app.py  voice.py  vision.py      # WP2
  a2ui.py                          # WP3: cards → A2UI messages
  agent.py  context.py  tools/sbb.py   # WP3
  fixtures/             # demo_reply.json, cards.json, screen.json, screen.png (WP2); context.json, *_a2ui.json (WP3)
  tests/
```

## One turn

The screenshot arrives before the question, so vision runs while the user is still talking.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant SC as Shortcut
  participant App as App (WP1)
  participant S as Server (WP2)
  participant V as Vision (WP2)
  participant G as Gradium
  participant A as Agent (WP3)
  SC->>S: POST /screenshot
  S->>V: read_screen(image), in the background
  V-->>S: ScreenContext
  S->>App: screen_ok {summary}
  App->>S: audio × n, then audio_end
  S->>G: stream mic audio, flush
  G-->>S: transcript segments
  S->>App: state thinking, transcript
  S->>A: turn(text, screen, on_status)
  A-->>S: on_status("Checking trains…")
  S->>App: state searching + label
  A-->>S: Reply {say, cards}
  S->>App: reply, a2ui, state speaking
  S->>G: TTS say
  G-->>S: audio chunks
  S->>App: audio × n, audio_end, state idle
```

## WebSocket `/ws`

JSON text frames only, one object per frame, discriminated by `type`. Audio is base64 inside JSON. The app sends `hello` first; the server closes the socket on a wrong token.

**App → server**

| `type` | Fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hello` | `token` | First frame after connecting |
| `audio` | `data`: base64 PCM, see [Audio](#audio) | Every 80 ms while the orb is held |
| `audio_end` | — | Orb released; the server finalizes STT and runs the turn |
| `text` | `text` | Typed question (debug field); runs a turn without STT |
| `screen` | `mime`, `data`: base64 | Optional: an image picked in the app, for rehearsals. Same effect as `POST /screenshot` |
| `interrupt` | — | Tap while the mascot is talking. Stops the current turn |

**Server → app**

| `type` | Fields | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | — | After a valid `hello` |
| `state` | `state`: `idle` \| `listening` \| `thinking` \| `searching` \| `speaking`; `label`?: string | On every change; `label` is the tool status, e.g. "Checking trains…" |
| `transcript` | `text` | Final transcript of the user's turn |
| `reply` | `say`, `cards`: see [Cards](#cards) | Before any of the turn's audio |
| `a2ui` | `messages`: list of A2UI v0.9 messages, see [A2UI](#a2ui) | Right after `reply`, when it has cards |
| `audio` | `data`: base64 PCM | TTS chunks for the last `reply` |
| `audio_end` | — | TTS for the last `reply` is complete |
| `screen_ok` | `summary`?: string | Vision has read a new screenshot; `summary` is missing if vision failed |
| `error` | `message` | Turn failed; the server then sends `state: idle` |

The orb shows `speaking` while the app still has audio queued, even after the server has sent `state: idle`.

**Interrupting.** A new press (its first `audio` frame), a `text`, or an `interrupt` cancels the running turn: the agent call and the TTS stream. A cancelled turn sends no `audio_end`. After `interrupt` the server sends `state: idle`; after a new press, `state: listening`. Gradium generates speech faster than real time, so seconds of audio may already be queued in the app. The app must stop playback the moment it interrupts, and drop `audio` frames until the next `reply`.

## HTTP

| Route | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `POST /screenshot` | From the iPhone Shortcut. `Authorization: Bearer <APP_TOKEN>`, body is the raw image (`image/jpeg` or `image/png`, max 8 MB). Returns `204` and starts vision |
| `GET /health` | `{"ok": true, "workspace": "rest" \| "fixture"}` |

**Screenshot rule:** the server keeps only the latest screenshot and its `ScreenContext`. A turn gets the context if the screenshot is less than 120 s old and no earlier turn has used it; if vision is still running, the turn waits for it.

## Audio

Both directions use Gradium's native format, so the server forwards the base64 strings without decoding them.

| Direction | Format | Gradium side |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mic, app → server | PCM signed 16-bit little-endian, mono, 24 kHz; 80 ms chunks = 1920 samples = 3840 bytes | STT setup `input_format: "pcm"` |
| TTS, server → app | Same format, chunks as Gradium sends them | TTS setup `output_format: "pcm_24000"` (the default `pcm` is 48 kHz) |

**iPhone side:** audio session `.playAndRecord` with `.defaultToSpeaker`, or iOS plays through the quiet earpiece while the mic is on. Turn on echo cancellation with `inputNode.setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true)` before reading the input format. Convert the input with `AVAudioConverter` to Int16 at 24 kHz mono. Play through an `AVAudioPlayerNode` on the same engine, converting each chunk to a Float32 24 kHz buffer.

**Gradium facts the server relies on** ([docs](https://docs.gradium.ai/api-reference/introduction)): auth header `x-api-key`; STT at `wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/asr`, TTS at `wss://api.gradium.ai/api/speech/tts`; the Python SDK is `pip install gradium`. STT needs `json_config.language` (`en` for the demo, `any` to auto-detect). STT sends `text` segments, not partial and final flags. On push-to-talk release the server sends `flush`, waits for `flushed`, and joins the segments into the transcript. TTS has no cancel message: closing the socket stops it. The free plan allows 2 TTS and 3 STT sessions at once, which is tight with 3 devs testing; the $13 XS plan raises that to 5 and 20.

## Cards

`reply.cards` holds 0 to 3 cards. The model fills them from tool results and context, and the server passes them through after validation. Optional fields may be missing. The app renders the `a2ui` messages built from these cards; native SwiftUI cards from `reply.cards` are the fallback.

| `kind` | Fields |
| --- | --- |
| `train` | `line` ("IC 8"), `from`, `to`, `departure`, `arrival`, `platform`?, `transfers`, `delay_min`? |
| `conflict` | `event` {`title`, `start`, `end`}, `proposal` {`title`, `start`, `place`?}, `verdict`: `fits` \| `tight` \| `clash`, `note`? |
| `event` | `title`, `start`, `end`, `location`?, `source`: `calendar` \| `luma` |
| `flight` | `flight_number`, `from`, `to` (IATA or city), `departure`, `arrival`, `booking_ref`? |

`fixtures/demo_reply.json`, the expected answer to the demo question:

```json
{
  "say": "Your call ends at quarter to six, and there's a train right after that gets you in just before seven.",
  "cards": [
    {
      "kind": "conflict",
      "event": {"title": "Call with Acme", "start": "2026-10-15T17:30:00+02:00", "end": "2026-10-15T17:45:00+02:00"},
      "proposal": {"title": "Dinner in Bern", "start": "2026-10-15T19:00:00+02:00", "place": "Bern"},
      "verdict": "fits",
      "note": "Leave right after the call"
    },
    {
      "kind": "train", "line": "IC 8", "from": "Zürich HB", "to": "Bern",
      "departure": "2026-10-15T18:01:00+02:00", "arrival": "2026-10-15T18:58:00+02:00",
      "platform": "31", "transfers": 0, "delay_min": 0
    }
  ]
}
```

`fixtures/cards.json` adds one card of each remaining kind, so every kind can be rendered:

```json
[
  {"kind": "event", "title": "Hackathon", "start": "2026-10-17T09:00:00+02:00", "end": "2026-10-18T18:00:00+02:00", "location": "Zürich", "source": "luma"},
  {"kind": "flight", "flight_number": "LX 1820", "from": "ZRH", "to": "LIS", "departure": "2026-10-20T07:10:00+02:00", "arrival": "2026-10-20T09:15:00+01:00", "booking_ref": "K7Q2ZP"}
]
```

Swift decoding: `keyDecodingStrategy = .convertFromSnakeCase`, `dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601`.

## A2UI

`a2ui.cards_to_a2ui(reply_id: str, cards: list[dict]) -> list[dict]` turns one reply into one surface, using only basic-catalog components so the app needs no custom Swift components:

```json
[
  {"version": "v0.9", "createSurface": {"surfaceId": "reply-3", "catalogId": "https://a2ui.org/specification/v0_9/basic_catalog.json"}},
  {"version": "v0.9", "updateComponents": {"surfaceId": "reply-3", "components": [
    {"id": "root", "component": "Column", "children": ["c0", "c1"]},
    {"id": "c1", "component": "Card", "child": "c1-body"},
    {"id": "c1-body", "component": "Column", "children": ["c1-time", "c1-line", "c1-meta"]},
    {"id": "c1-time", "component": "Text", "text": "18:01 → 18:58", "variant": "h2"},
    {"id": "c1-line", "component": "Text", "text": "IC 8 · Zürich HB → Bern"},
    {"id": "c1-meta", "component": "Text", "text": "Platform 31 · direct", "variant": "caption"}
  ]}}
]
```

(`c0`, the conflict card, is left out above for brevity.) Rules:

- Use the catalog id exactly as written. It's a2ui-swift's `basicCatalogId`; the React renderer uses a different one.
- Format times as `HH:MM` in Europe/Zurich on the server, so the app doesn't need A2UI format functions.
- Use a new `surfaceId` per reply, and one `SurfaceViewModel(catalog: basicCatalog)` per surface in the app.
- No buttons or actions in the MVP.

## Screen context

What WP2's vision step produces and WP3's agent consumes. `vision.read_screen(image: bytes, mime: str) -> dict` makes one Gemini call with structured output (`response_json_schema`), passing the current time so relative dates resolve. `fixtures/screen.json`:

```json
{
  "app": "WhatsApp",
  "summary": "Anna asks about dinner in Bern on Thursday at 7.",
  "messages": [{"from": "Anna", "text": "Dinner in Bern Thursday at 7?"}],
  "proposal": {"title": "Dinner", "date": "2026-10-15", "time": "19:00", "place": "Bern"}
}
```

`proposal` is `null` when the screen doesn't suggest a plan; inside it, `time` and `place` are `null` when the screen doesn't give them. `from` is the sender's name as shown, or `"Me"` for the phone owner's own messages. Vision copies on-screen text as data and never acts on it. The agent puts the whole object in its prompt marked as untrusted, and never follows instructions inside it.

## Agent interface

What WP2's server calls and WP3 implements in `agent.py`. WP2's `StubAgent` has the same shape and returns `demo_reply.json`.

```python
from typing import Awaitable, Callable, TypedDict

class Reply(TypedDict):

The server already handles that frame like a screenshot, so the contract doesn't change. """Stand-in for the iPhone app: speaks a WAV file (or types text) into /ws and
prints what comes back. The mascot's answer is saved to reply.wav.

From backend/, with the server running:
    uv run python fake_app.py out.wav
    uv run python fake_app.py --text "Can I make it?"
    uv run python fake_app.py out.wav --url wss://<tunnel>/ws
    uv run python fake_app.py --text "Can I make it?" --interrupt-after 1.0
    uv run python fake_app.py out.wav --handsfree    # then 3 s of silence and no audio_end
"""

import argparse
import array
import asyncio
import base64
import json
import os
import ssl
import time
import wave

import certifi
import websockets
from dotenv import load_dotenv

CHUNK_BYTES = 3840  # 80 ms of 24 kHz s16 mono


def speech_end(pcm: bytes) -> int:
    """Byte offset just past the last chunk with a sample louder than -36 dBFS."""
    samples = array.array("h", pcm)
    last = max((i for i, x in enumerate(samples) if abs(x) > 500), default=0)
    return (last * 2 // CHUNK_BYTES + 1) * CHUNK_BYTES


async def mic(ws, pcm: bytes) -> None:
    for i in range(0, len(pcm), CHUNK_BYTES):  # paced like a live mic
        chunk = base64.b64encode(pcm[i : i + CHUNK_BYTES]).decode()
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "audio", "data": chunk}))
        await asyncio.sleep(0.08)


async def main(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    tls = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()) if args.url.startswith("wss") else None
    async with websockets.connect(args.url, max_size=None, ssl=tls) as ws:
        mode = {"mode": "handsfree"} if args.handsfree else {}
        await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "hello", "token": os.environ["APP_TOKEN"]} | mode))
        print(json.loads(await ws.recv()))
        silence = None
        if args.text:
            await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "text", "text": args.text}))
        else:
            with wave.open(args.wav, "rb") as f:
                pcm = f.readframes(f.getnframes())
            if args.handsfree:  # the mic stays open; the server hears the end of the turn
                end = speech_end(pcm)  # TTS WAVs trail off in silence; time from the last word
                await mic(ws, pcm[:end])
                silence = asyncio.create_task(mic(ws, pcm[end:] + bytes(3 * 24000 * 2)))
            else:
                await mic(ws, pcm)
                await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "audio_end"}))
        released = time.monotonic()
        audio, first_audio, transcript = bytearray(), None, None
        while True:
            msg = json.loads(await ws.recv())
            if msg["type"] == "transcript":
                transcript = time.monotonic() - released
            if msg["type"] == "audio":
                if first_audio is None:
                    first_audio = time.monotonic() - released
                    if args.interrupt_after is not None:
                        asyncio.get_running_loop().call_later(
                            args.interrupt_after,
                            lambda: asyncio.ensure_future(ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "interrupt"}))),
                        )
                audio += base64.b64decode(msg["data"])
                continue
            print(f"{time.monotonic() - released:5.2f}s", json.dumps(msg, ensure_ascii=False)[:160])
            if msg == {"type": "state", "state": "idle"}:
                break
        if silence is not None:
            silence.cancel()
        with wave.open("reply.wav", "wb") as f:
            f.setnchannels(1)
            f.setsampwidth(2)
            f.setframerate(24000)
            f.writeframes(bytes(audio))
        if transcript is not None:
            print(f"transcript {transcript:.2f}s after end of speech")
        if first_audio is not None:
            print(f"first audio {first_audio:.2f}s after end of speech; reply.wav is {len(audio) / 48000:.1f}s")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    load_dotenv()
    load_dotenv("../.env")
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("wav", nargs="?")
    p.add_argument("--text")
    p.add_argument("--url", default="ws://localhost:8000/ws")
    p.add_argument("--interrupt-after", type=float, help="seconds after first audio")
    p.add_argument("--handsfree", action="store_true", help="hello with mode handsfree, no audio_end")
    asyncio.run(main(p.parse_args()))

def token_ok(token: object) -> bool:
    expected = os.environ.get("APP_TOKEN", "")
    return bool(expected) and isinstance(token, str) and hmac.compare_digest(token, expected)


async def broadcast(msg: dict) -> None:
    for session in list(sessions):
        try:
            await session.send(msg)
        except Exception:
            log.warning("could not send %s to a session", msg["type"])


async def read_latest(shot: Screenshot) -> dict | None:
    """Run vision on one screenshot, tell every session, return its ScreenContext or None."""
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    screen = None
    if read_screen is None:
        log.warning("vision.py not available, screenshot %d not read", shot.id)
    else:
        try:
            if inspect.iscoroutinefunction(read_screen):
                screen = await read_screen(shot.image, shot.mime)
            else:  # a sync read_screen must not block the event loop
                screen = await asyncio.to_thread(read_screen, shot.image, shot.mime)
        except Exception:
            log.exception("vision failed on screenshot %d", shot.id)
        screen = screen if isinstance(screen, dict) else None
    summary = screen.get("summary") if screen else None
    log.info("screenshot %d read in %.2fs: %r", shot.id, time.monotonic() - t0, summary)
    await broadcast({"type": "screen_ok"} | ({"summary": summary} if summary else {}))
    return screen


def store_screenshot(image: bytes, mime: str) -> None:
    """Keep only the latest screenshot and start reading it."""
    global latest
    if latest and latest.task:
        latest.task.cancel()  # its context is stale now
    latest = Screenshot(latest.id + 1 if latest else 1, image, mime, time.monotonic())
    latest.task = asyncio.create_task(read_latest(latest))
    log.info("screenshot %d: %d bytes %s", latest.id, len(image), mime)


async def take_screen() -> tuple[Screenshot | None, dict | None]:
    """The latest screenshot and its ScreenContext if fresh and unused (contracts § HTTP).

    The caller marks it used once its turn completes, so a turn the user interrupts
    leaves the screen for the question they ask next."""
    shot = latest
    if shot is None or shot.used or time.monotonic() - shot.at > SCREEN_MAX_AGE:
        return None, None
    await asyncio.wait({shot.task}, timeout=VISION_WAIT)  # never cancels the vision task
    if not shot.task.done() or shot.task.cancelled():
        log.warning("screenshot %d not read within %ds, turn goes without it", shot.id, VISION_WAIT)
        return None, None
    return shot, shot.task.result()

async def screenshot(request: Request) -> Response:
    scheme, _, token = request.headers.get("authorization", "").partition(" ")
    if scheme.lower() != "bearer" or not token_ok(token):
        raise HTTPException(401)
    mime = request.headers.get("content-type", "").split(";")[0].strip().lower()
    if mime not in SCREEN_MIMES:

    image = bytearray()
    async for chunk in request.stream():  # count bytes; Content-Length can lie

    store_screenshot(bytes(image), mime)

class Session:
    def __init__(self, ws: WebSocket, handsfree: bool = False):
        self.ws = ws
        self.agent = make_agent()
        self.turns = 0
        self.stt: voice.Transcriber | None = None
        self.listener = voice.ContinuousTranscriber(self.heard_speech, self.heard_turn) if handsfree else None
        self.turn_task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self._send_lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def send(self, msg: dict) -> None:
        async with self._send_lock:
            await self.ws.send_json(msg)

    async def state(self, state: str, label: str | None = None) -> None:
        await self.send({"type": "state", "state": state} | ({"label": label} if label else {}))

    async def run_turn(self, text: str, timings: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> None:
        self.turns += 1
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        timings = timings or {}
        await self.state("thinking")

        async def on_status(label: str) -> None:
            await self.state("searching", label)

        shot, screen = await take_screen()
        timings["vision_wait"] = time.monotonic() - t0
        t_agent = time.monotonic()
        try:
            reply = await self.agent.turn(text, screen, on_status)
        except Exception:
            log.exception("turn failed")
            await self.send({"type": "error", "message": "Sorry, something went wrong."})
            await self.state("idle")
            return
        timings["agent"] = time.monotonic() - t_agent
        if shot is not None:
            shot.used = True

        await self.send({"type": "reply", "say": reply["say"], "cards": reply["cards"]})
        if cards_to_a2ui and reply["cards"]:
            messages = cards_to_a2ui(f"reply-{self.turns}", reply["cards"])
            await self.send({"type": "a2ui", "messages": messages})
        await self.state("speaking")
        try:
            async for chunk in voice.speak(reply["say"]):
                timings.setdefault("first_audio", time.monotonic() - t0)
                await self.send({"type": "audio", "data": chunk})
        except Exception:
            log.exception("TTS failed")  # the reply text and cards are already on screen
        await self.send({"type": "audio_end"})
        await self.state("idle")
        timings["total"] = time.monotonic() - t0
        log.info("turn %d %r timings %s", self.turns, text, {k: round(v, 2) for k, v in timings.items()})

    async def voice_turn(self, stt: voice.Transcriber) -> None:
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            text = await stt.finish()
        except Exception:
            log.exception("STT failed")
            text = ""
        if not text:
            await self.send({"type": "error", "message": "Sorry, I didn't catch that."})
            await self.state("idle")
            return
        await self.send({"type": "transcript", "text": text})
        await self.run_turn(text, {"stt": time.monotonic() - t0})

    async def heard_speech(self) -> None:
        """Hands-free: the user's first words of a turn; talking over the mascot interrupts it."""
        await self.interrupt()
        await self.state("listening")

    async def heard_turn(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Hands-free: Gradium's VAD says the user is done."""
        await self.interrupt()
        await self.send({"type": "transcript", "text": text})
        self.start_turn(self.run_turn(text))

    def start_turn(self, coro) -> None:
        """Turns run as tasks so the receive loop can still hear an interrupt."""
        self.turn_task = asyncio.create_task(coro)

    async def interrupt(self) -> bool:
        """Cancel the running turn: the agent call and the TTS socket. True if one was running."""
        task, self.turn_task = self.turn_task, None
        if task is None or task.done():
            return False
        task.cancel()
        try:
            await task
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            pass
        log.info("turn %d interrupted", self.turns)
        return True

    async def handle(self, msg: dict) -> None:
        kind = msg.get("type")
        if kind == "audio" and self.listener is not None and isinstance(msg.get("data"), str):
            self.listener.push(msg["data"])  # hands-free: the mic never stops, no audio_end
        elif kind == "audio" and isinstance(msg.get("data"), str):
            if self.stt is None:  # a new press; talking over the mascot interrupts it
                await self.interrupt()
                self.stt = voice.Transcriber()
                await self.state("listening")
            self.stt.push(msg["data"])
        elif kind == "audio_end" and self.stt is not None:
            stt, self.stt = self.stt, None
            self.start_turn(self.voice_turn(stt))
        elif kind == "text" and isinstance(msg.get("text"), str):
            await self.interrupt()
            self.start_turn(self.run_turn(msg["text"]))
        elif kind == "screen":
            try:
                image = base64.b64decode(msg.get("data"), validate=True)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                image = b""
            if msg.get("mime") in SCREEN_MIMES and 0 < len(image) <= SCREEN_MAX_BYTES:
                store_screenshot(image, msg["mime"])
            else:
                log.warning("ignored screen frame: bad mime, base64 or size")
        elif kind == "interrupt":
            if await self.interrupt():
                await self.state("idle")
        else:
            log.warning("ignored message type %r", kind)

    def close(self) -> None:
        if self.stt is not None:
            self.stt.cancel()
        if self.listener is not None:
            self.listener.cancel()
        if self.turn_task is not None:
            self.turn_task.cancel()

class TurnDetector:
    """Hands-free end of turn: inactivity_prob at END_HORIZON_S above END_PROB for
    END_STEPS `step`s in a row, counted only once the turn has text."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.words: list[str] = []
        self._streak = 0

    def feed(self, msg: dict) -> bool:
        """One STT message in; True when the turn has ended."""
        if msg["type"] == "text" and msg["text"].strip():
            self.words.append(msg["text"].strip())
        elif msg["type"] == "step" and self.words:
            p = next((v["inactivity_prob"] for v in msg["vad"] if v["horizon_s"] == END_HORIZON_S), 0.0)
            self._streak = self._streak + 1 if p > END_PROB else 0
            return self._streak >= END_STEPS
        return False

    def take(self) -> str:
        """The turn's text; starts the next turn."""
        text, self.words, self._streak = " ".join(self.words), [], 0
        return text


class ContinuousTranscriber:
    """Hands-free: one STT session per WebSocket, open across turns. push() base64 chunks
    for as long as the mic is on. Awaits on_speech() at a turn's first words and
    on_turn(text) at its end. If Gradium closes the session, the next push() reopens it."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        on_speech: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]],
        on_turn: Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]],
        language: str = "en",
    ):
        self._on_speech, self._on_turn, self._language = on_speech, on_turn, language
        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[bytes] = asyncio.Queue()
        self._task: asyncio.Task | None = None
        self._opened = float("-inf")

    def push(self, b64: str) -> None:
        closed = self._task is None or self._task.done()
        if closed and time.monotonic() - self._opened > REOPEN_AFTER_S:
            self._opened = time.monotonic()
            self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run())
        self._queue.put_nowait(base64.b64decode(b64))

    def cancel(self) -> None:
        if self._task is not None:
            self._task.cancel()

    async def _run(self) -> None:
        try:
            async with client().stt_realtime(
                model_name="default", input_format="pcm", json_config={"language": self._language}
            ) as stt:

                async def send() -> None:
                    while True:
                        await stt.send_audio(await self._queue.get())

                sender = asyncio.create_task(send())
                try:
                    await self._listen(stt)
                finally:
                    sender.cancel()
        except Exception:
            log.exception("hands-free STT failed")
        log.info("hands-free STT session closed; the next audio reopens it")

    async def _listen(self, stt) -> None:
        turn, flushing = TurnDetector(), False
        async for msg in _messages(stt):
            fresh = not turn.words
            ended = turn.feed(msg)
            if fresh and turn.words:
                await self._on_speech()
            if ended and not flushing:  # flush makes Gradium emit the words it holds back
                flushing = True
                await stt.send_flush()
            elif msg["type"] == "flushed" and flushing:
                flushing = False
                await self._on_turn(turn.take())

Yes, and it's already built. Hands-free mode was added to this branch in the last few commits (`47b88aa`, `bed7559`, `647358c`). I just tested it on your Mac. The client never sent `audio_end`, and the server worked out on its own when I'd stopped talking:

```
 0.00s listening
 0.87s transcript "Can I make it to dinner and burn?"
 1.87s reply + speaking
 5.00s idle
first audio 2.06s after end of speech
```

**How it works:**
- The app sends `hello` with `"mode": "handsfree"` and then streams the mic the whole time it's connected, including while the mascot is talking. Push-to-talk stays the default.
- The server keeps one Gradium STT session open per connection. It ends a turn when Gradium's voice detection is fairly sure you've stopped: `inactivity_prob` above 0.5 for 3 steps in a row. Then it runs the turn as usual.
- If you talk over the mascot, the server cancels the turn and sends `state: listening`. That's the app's cue to stop playback at once.

**What the iPhone (WP1) has to get right:**
- **Echo cancellation:** `setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true)` must stay on. Otherwise the mic hears the mascot on the loudspeaker and it cuts itself off.
- **Gradium session limit:** each connected phone holds an STT session the whole time, even in silence. The free plan allows only 3 at once, so with 3 devs testing you'll hit it. The $13 plan raises it to 20.
- **App in the background:** iOS stops the mic once the app leaves the foreground. To keep it on you need the `audio` background mode, and the orange mic dot stays on.

**One problem in this run:** "on Thursday" was cut off the transcript. In push-to-talk the same WAV gave the full sentence. Either the turn ended after "burn" and the last words went to a next turn that never finished, or the flush lost them. Worth checking before you rely on hands-free for the demo.

```bash
uv run python fake_app.py out.wav --handsfree

# Gemini Live API Development Skill

## Overview

The Live API enables **low-latency, real-time voice and video interactions** with Gemini over WebSockets. It processes continuous streams of audio, video, or text to deliver immediate, human-like spoken responses and background reasoning.

Key capabilities:
- **Bidirectional audio streaming** — real-time mic-to-speaker conversations
- **Background reasoning (extended thinking)** — multi-step background reasoning with spoken conversational fillers
- **Live streaming transcription** — real-time speech-to-text with interim and finalized streams
- **Video streaming** — send camera/screen frames alongside audio
- **Text input/output** — send and receive text within a live session
- **Audio transcriptions** — get text transcripts of both input and output audio
- **Voice Activity Detection (VAD)** — automatic server VAD, client-side Hybrid VAD, and manual Push-to-Talk
- **Asynchronous function calling** — non-blocking tool execution while audio continues streaming
- **Full-session client content** — inject and update conversation turns mid-stream
- **Session management** — context compression, session resumption, GoAway signals
- **Ephemeral tokens** — secure client-side authentication

> [!NOTE]
> The Live API connects directly via **WebSockets**. For WebRTC support or simplified integration, use a [partner integration](#partner-integrations).

## Models

### Current Models (Use These)

- `gemini-3.8-live` — Default option for most low-latency voice agent experiences and real-time dialogue without reasoning delays. Supports interleaved reasoning, asynchronous function calling by default (`behavior: NON_BLOCKING`), and full-session client content updates.
- `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking` — High-reasoning audio-to-audio model recommended when higher background reasoning is required during live interactions. Processes background reasoning and async tool calls (`behavior: NON_BLOCKING` required) while streaming continuous spoken conversational fillers; lifecycle managed via `interaction_status` (`IN_PROGRESS` vs `IDLE`).
- `gemini-3.5-transcribe-live` — Real-time streaming speech-to-text with interim hypotheses, finalized transcripts, smart formatting, and Hybrid VAD.
- `gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` — Real-time speech-to-speech streaming translation across 70+ languages.

> [!WARNING]
> **Legacy Models (`gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`, `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-*`, `gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview`, `gemini-2.0-flash-live-001`)**: Read [`references/migration.md`](references/migration.md) for breaking protocol changes (`behavior: "NON_BLOCKING"`, `thinking_level`, `interaction_status`, `send_client_content`).

## SDKs

- **Python**: `google-genai` >= `2.3.0` — `pip install -U google-genai`
- **JavaScript/TypeScript**: `@google/genai` >= `2.3.0` — `npm install @google/genai`

> [!WARNING]
> Legacy SDKs `google-generativeai` (Python) and `@google/generative-ai` (JS) are **deprecated**. Never use them.

## Partner Integrations

To streamline real-time audio/video app development, use a third-party integration supporting the Gemini Live API over **WebRTC** or **WebSockets**:

- [LiveKit](https://docs.livekit.io/agents/models/realtime/plugins/gemini/) — Use the Gemini Live API with LiveKit Agents.
- [Pipecat by Daily](https://docs.pipecat.ai/guides/features/gemini-live) — Create a real-time AI chatbot using Gemini Live and Pipecat.
- [Fishjam by Software Mansion](https://docs.fishjam.io/tutorials/gemini-live-integration) — Create live video and audio streaming applications with Fishjam.
- [Vision Agents by Stream](https://visionagents.ai/integrations/gemini) — Build real-time voice and video AI applications with Vision Agents.
- [Voximplant](https://voximplant.com/products/gemini-client) — Connect inbound and outbound calls to Live API with Voximplant.
- [Firebase AI SDK](https://firebase.google.com/docs/ai-logic/live-api?api=dev) — Get started with the Gemini Live API using Firebase AI Logic.

## Audio Formats

- **Input**: Raw PCM, little-endian, 16-bit, mono. 16kHz native (will resample others). MIME type: `audio/pcm;rate=16000`
- **Output**: Raw PCM, little-endian, 16-bit, mono. 24kHz sample rate.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Use `send_realtime_input` / `sendRealtimeInput` for all real-time streaming user input (audio, video, **and text**). On Gemini 3.8 models, `send_client_content` / `sendClientContent` is supported across the full session lifecycle with explicit roles (`user` or `model`) to inject conversation context (`turn_complete=true` unconditionally interrupts active generation).

> [!WARNING]
> Do **not** use `media` in `sendRealtimeInput`. Use the specific keys: `audio` for audio data, `video` for images/video frames, and `text` for text input.

---

## Quick Start

### Authentication

#### Python

```python
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(api_key="YOUR_API_KEY")
```

#### JavaScript

```js
import { GoogleGenAI } from '@google/genai';

const ai = new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: 'YOUR_API_KEY' });
```

### Connecting to the Live API

#### Python
```python
from google.genai import types

config = types.LiveConnectConfig(
    response_modalities=[types.Modality.AUDIO],
    system_instruction=types.Content(
        parts=[types.Part(text="You are a helpful assistant.")]
    )
)

async with client.aio.live.connect(model="gemini-3.8-live", config=config) as session:
    pass  # Session is active
```

#### JavaScript
```js
const session = await ai.live.connect({
  model: 'gemini-3.8-live',
  config: {
    responseModalities: ['audio'],
    systemInstruction: { parts: [{ text: 'You are a helpful assistant.' }] }
  },
  callbacks: {
    onopen: () => console.log('Connected'),
    onmessage: (response) => console.log('Message:', response),
    onerror: (error) => console.error('Error:', error),
    onclose: () => console.log('Closed')
  }
});
```

### Sending Text

#### Python
```python
await session.send_realtime_input(text="Hello, how are you?")
```

#### JavaScript
```js
session.sendRealtimeInput({ text: 'Hello, how are you?' });
```

### Sending Audio

#### Python
```python
await session.send_realtime_input(
    audio=types.Blob(data=chunk, mime_type="audio/pcm;rate=16000")
)
```

#### JavaScript
```js
session.sendRealtimeInput({
  audio: { data: chunk.toString('base64'), mimeType: 'audio/pcm;rate=16000' }
});
```

### Sending Video

#### Python
```python
# frame: raw JPEG-encoded bytes
await session.send_realtime_input(
    video=types.Blob(data=frame, mime_type="image/jpeg")
)
```

#### JavaScript
```js
session.sendRealtimeInput({
  video: { data: frame.toString('base64'), mimeType: 'image/jpeg' }
});
```

### Receiving Audio and Text

> [!IMPORTANT]
> A single server event can contain **multiple content parts simultaneously** (e.g., audio chunks and transcript). Always process **all** parts in each event to avoid missing content.

#### Python
```python
async for response in session.receive():
    content = response.server_content
    if content:
        # Audio — process ALL parts in each event
        if content.model_turn:
            for part in content.model_turn.parts:
                if part.inline_data:
                    audio_data = part.inline_data.data
        # Transcription
        if content.input_transcription:
            print(f"User: {content.input_transcription.text}")
        if content.output_transcription:
            print(f"Gemini: {content.output_transcription.text}")
        # Interruption
        if content.interrupted is True:
            pass  # Stop playback, clear audio queue
```

#### JavaScript
```js
// Inside the onmessage callback
const content = response.serverContent;
if (content?.modelTurn?.parts) {
  for (const part of content.modelTurn.parts) {
    if (part.inlineData) {
      const audioData = part.inlineData.data; // Base64 encoded
    }
  }
}
if (content?.inputTranscription) console.log('User:', content.inputTranscription.text);
if (content?.outputTranscription) console.log('Gemini:', content.outputTranscription.text);
if (content?.interrupted) { /* Stop playback, clear audio queue */ }
```

---

## Background Reasoning (Extended Thinking)

Use `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking` when your voice agent must evaluate complex data, plan multiple steps, or handle long-running tools. The model speaks natural conversational fillers (e.g. *"Checking flight options now..."*) while executing asynchronous tools in the background.

Key requirements:
- **Thinking config**: Set `thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_level="low")` (`"minimal"` | `"low"` | `"medium"` | `"high"`).
- **Non-blocking tools**: All function declarations **must** set `behavior="NON_BLOCKING"`. Synchronous blocking mode is not supported and returns an error.
- **Lifecycle tracking (`interaction_status`)**: Do **not** rely on `turn_complete=True` alone to detect turn completion. Monitor `message.interaction_status` (Python) / `message.interactionStatus` (JS):
  - `"IN_PROGRESS"`: Server is reasoning, speaking conversational fillers, or waiting for async tool responses.
  - `"IDLE"`: Server has completed all background reasoning and tool calls; session is ready for user input.

See [`references/migration.md`](references/migration.md) and the [Thinking in Live API Guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/thinking.md.txt) for complete Python and JavaScript implementation examples.

---

## Live Translation (Gemini Live Translate)

The Live API supports real-time, low-latency streaming translation of speech (audio) across 70+ languages. For full details on options and capabilities, see the [Live Translate Guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/live-translate.md.txt).

### Model
- `gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` — The recommended translation model for all Live Translate use cases.

### Configuration (`TranslationConfig`)

To enable translation, specify a `TranslationConfig` object inside your live session setup:

- **Python SDK**: Configure the connection using `translation_config` on `LiveConnectConfig`:
  ```python
  config = types.LiveConnectConfig(
      response_modalities=[types.Modality.AUDIO],
      translation_config=types.TranslationConfig(
          target_language_code="es",  # Target language code (e.g. es, fr, pl)
          echo_target_language=True,
      ),
      input_audio_transcription=types.AudioTranscriptionConfig(),
      output_audio_transcription=types.AudioTranscriptionConfig(),
  )
  ```
- **Raw WebSockets**: Place `translationConfig` inside `generationConfig`:
  ```json
  {
    "setup": {
      "model": "models/gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview",
      "generationConfig": {
        "responseModalities": ["AUDIO"],
        "translationConfig": {
          "targetLanguageCode": "es",
          "echoTargetLanguage": true
        }
      }
    }
  }
  ```

---

## Live Streaming Transcription (Gemini Live Transcribe)

The Live API supports real-time streaming speech-to-text over WebSockets with low-latency interim hypotheses, finalized transcripts, and Hybrid VAD. For full details, see the [Live Transcription Guide](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api/live-transcribe.md.txt) and [Colab Cookbook](https://colab.research.google.com/github/google-gemini/cookbook/blob/main/quickstarts/Get_started_transcribe.ipynb).

### Model
- `gemini-3.5-transcribe-live`

### Modes
- `smart`: cleans up filler words, resolves inline self-corrections, and structures formatting.
- `verbatim` (default): exact word-for-word transcript.

### Python
```python
config = types.LiveConnectConfig(
    response_modalities=["TEXT"],
    input_audio_transcription=types.AudioTranscriptionConfig(),
)

async with client.aio.live.connect(model="gemini-3.5-transcribe-live", config=config) as session:

    await session.send_realtime_input(audio=types.Blob(data=chunk, mime_type="audio/pcm;rate=16000"))
    # Hybrid VAD: notify turn end on client-detected silence for zero latency
    await session.send_realtime_input(audio_stream_end=True)

## Limitations

- **Response modality** — Only `TEXT` **or** `AUDIO` per session, not both. Native audio models output audio (`response_modalities=["AUDIO"]`); enable `output_audio_transcription` if you need text transcripts.

Partly. Feeding in Gradium's transcript works, but having Gradium speak the answer doesn't fit well.

- **Gradium STT in: works.** You stream the screen frames into the Live session and send each Gradium transcript in as text with `send_realtime_input(text=…)`. Gemini sees the screen and reads your question.
- **Gradium TTS out: only with a workaround.** `gemini-3.8-live` can only answer in audio; the migration guide says audio is its only output. To get Gradium's voice you would have to:
  - throw away Gemini's audio and have Gradium re-speak Gemini's transcript, which adds Gradium's latency on top of Gemini's audio, or
  - make Gemini answer through a `respond(say, cards)` tool and ignore its voice. But Live's proactive audio is always on, so while it watches your screen it may start talking by itself.

  Either way you pay for audio you discard and fight the model's design.

**Better fit: get Gemini's video understanding without the Live socket.** Keep the pipeline as it is: Gradium STT → agent on `gemini-3.8-flash` → Gradium TTS. Give the agent the last 5–10 s of your screen as video:
- **Capture:** the Mac records the screen continuously into a short rolling clip (ffmpeg) or keeps frames at 1 per second.
- **Read:** when you start talking, the server sends that clip or those frames to Gemini in one call.
- **Gemini:** it understands the video, as in Live, but answers in text. That fits our `say` + cards and the mascot voice.
- **Contract:** stays the same. The screen context just comes from a clip instead of one screenshot.

What you give up compared with Live: Gemini doesn't comment on its own while you work, and it only looks when you speak. For "can I make it to dinner?" that's what you want anyway.

# Screen clip: the last seconds of the Mac screen, not one frame

Sub-packages of WP2, on branch `feature/wp2-screen-clip` (from `develop`). Today the Mac prototype client (`backend/static/index.html`) sends one screen frame when a question starts. After this, it sends the current frame plus the frames from the last ~10 seconds, and vision reads them in one Gemini call. The agent then knows what the user just looked at, even after they switched to the calendar to check.

The pipeline stays as it is: Gradium STT → agent → Gradium TTS. The iPhone keeps the Action Button screenshot.

## Decisions

| Question | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gemini Live or the existing pipeline? | Existing pipeline, `generate_content` | Live (`gemini-3.8-live`) only answers in audio, so we'd lose the Gradium mascot voice and the `say` + cards reply. Audio+video sessions also end after 2 min without compression |
| Video file or frames? | JPEG frames, about 1 per second | Gemini samples video at 1 fps anyway, so the frames are the same input without encoding an mp4. The browser already has the frames from `getDisplayMedia` |
| Where is the ring buffer? | In the browser; it sends the frames when a question starts | Frames are uploaded once per turn, not continuously through the tunnel. The server keeps its "latest screenshot" model |
| When does vision run? | When the question starts: press, first words in hands-free, or `text` | The same trigger as today, so vision overlaps the user's speech |
| Shape of the result | `ScreenContext`, unchanged | WP3 needs no code change. `summary` and `messages` may now cover earlier frames |

## Contract change

This lands in `docs/contracts.md` in the same commit as SC2 (team rule: contracts first, with the code that needs them).

- **`screen` frame (app → server):** new optional field `recent`, a list of base64 images with the same `mime`. They are the earlier frames, oldest first, about 1 s apart, up to 9. `data` stays the current frame. A `screen` without `recent` works exactly as before.
- **Limits:** each image is at most `SCREEN_MAX_BYTES`; all images together are at most 8 MB decoded. If `recent` is malformed or over the limit, the server drops `recent` and keeps `data`. It never drops the current frame.
- **Vision:** `read_screen(image, mime, now=None, earlier=())`. `earlier` is a list of image bytes, oldest first. The return value is the same `ScreenContext`:
  - `messages` covers all frames, deduplicated, oldest first.
  - `proposal` comes from the newest frame that shows one.
  - `summary` describes the current screen and may mention what was seen just before.
- **Screen content:** all frames are untrusted data, as today.

## Packages
